classification.difficultyReason: With elimination specified, select a variable and coefficient multipliers, decide whether to add or subtract the scaled equations and substitute back; the hardest pairs require scaling both equations.

content.prompt: Use the elimination method to solve the following pairs of simultaneous equations.

answer.worked:
Adding the equations eliminates $y$.

$$\begin{align*}3x&=9\\x&=3\end{align*}$$

Substitute into $x-y=5$.

$$\begin{align*}3-y&=5\\-y&=2\\y&=-2\end{align*}$$

Check: $2(3)+(-2)=4$ and $3-(-2)=5$.

Multiply the second equation by $2$.

$$2x-2y=4$$

Subtract this from the first equation.

$$\begin{align*}3x&=-1\\x&=-\frac13\end{align*}$$

Substitute into $x-y=2$.

$$\begin{align*}-\frac13-y&=2\\-y&=\frac73\\y&=-\frac73\end{align*}$$

Check: $5(-\frac13)-2(-\frac73)=3$ and $-\frac13-(-\frac73)=2$.

Multiply the first equation by $4$ and the second by $3$.

$$\begin{aligned}8x+12y&=32\\9x-12y&=30\end{aligned}$$

Adding eliminates $y$.

$$\begin{align*}17x&=62\\x&=\frac{62}{17}\end{align*}$$

Substitute into $2x+3y=8$.

$$\begin{align*}2\left(\frac{62}{17}\right)+3y&=8\\3y&=\frac{12}{17}\\y&=\frac4{17}\end{align*}$$

Check: $2(\frac{62}{17})+3(\frac4{17})=8$ and $3(\frac{62}{17})-4(\frac4{17})=10$.

Multiply the first equation by $2$ and the second by $5$.

$$\begin{aligned}10x-8y&=26\\10x-35y&=30\end{aligned}$$

Subtract the second scaled equation from the first.

$$\begin{align*}27y&=-4\\y&=-\frac4{27}\end{align*}$$

Substitute into $2x-7y=6$.

$$\begin{align*}2x-7\left(-\frac4{27}\right)&=6\\2x&=\frac{134}{27}\\x&=\frac{67}{27}\end{align*}$$

Check: $5(\frac{67}{27})-4(-\frac4{27})=13$ and $2(\frac{67}{27})-7(-\frac4{27})=6$.
